t: The 32-bit chip inside the Arduino Due, built for USB, audio, and car data.
steps: Buy an Arduino Due from a distributor, or a Due-compatible clone from a maker store.
Install the free Arduino IDE on your computer.
Open the Boards Manager and add the Arduino SAM Boards package.
Plug a micro-USB cable into the programming port next to the power jack.
Choose Arduino Due Programming Port in the board menu.
Open the Blink example and press Upload. The onboard LED starts to blink.
Use 3.3 volt sensors and shields from here on to protect the pins.
